LHX.sentence: L3Harris ticked up a little, and while its profit margins look thin right now, that's likely a one-time charge rather than anything broken in the business — defense spending remains a steady tailwind for the smallest of the big five military contractors.

ASML.sentence: ASML is quiet — it's still the only company on earth that makes the machines needed to print the most advanced chips, and after last year's run the price has cooled to a more reasonable level.

LIN.sentence: Linde is having a completely flat week — they supply oxygen, nitrogen and other industrial gases under long contracts and nudge prices up steadily, and right now it's trading at an unusually fair price for such a dependable operator.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft has quietly pulled way ahead of the other tech giants over the past month, as its Azure cloud business keeps powering the AI boom without any drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher dipped a touch, but biotech funding is thawing and that money tends to show up in their lab-equipment orders a couple of quarters later, so the backdrop is quietly improving.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge is steady — this Canadian pipeline company works like a toll road for oil and gas and pays a hefty dividend, which is really the whole reason to own it.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow had a strong week and has been outrunning its peers, as big companies and government agencies keep signing up for its AI workflow tools — though after such a sharp run the shares are looking a bit stretched.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore slipped a bit as copper prices wobbled, but nothing unusual is happening — this miner and commodity trader is sitting right in the middle of its normal cycle.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta fell a bit and its headline price-per-ton looks like it dropped, but that's just a shift in the mix of products sold — the real price of crushed stone is still climbing about 4%, which is the part that matters for this quarry business.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA drifted down slightly, though a strong Mexican peso helps when its Latin American sales get converted back to dollars — otherwise a quiet week for the region's biggest Coke bottler.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras jumped a few percent on cooperative oil prices, but its earnings look like they're near a peak, so this is a good stretch that may not last.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, has climbed sharply on a spike in freight rates — that run looks stretched, even though the shares are still priced below the company's underlying worth.

MA.sentence: Mastercard dipped a little, but oddly it's now priced slightly cheaper than its twin Visa, which almost never happens — meanwhile people keep tapping their cards more than ever, so the business itself is fine.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical robot maker is down heavily from its high — a steep fall for such a dominant company — even as hospitals keep doing more operations with its machines, each of which sells more disposable instruments.
